This isn't really saying much. Slysoft "broke" BD+ a while ago. Then they "broke" it again, and "again" after that. Each time they "break" it, Macrovision revs up the protection code and "breaks" Slysoft.

Slysoft is far ahead of Doom9 in this effort, and they get paid to do it. There are disks today that AnyDVD still can't play.

Both Slysoft and Doom9 are emulating the BD+ VM. It is obviously possible to emulate any instruction set architecture. The question is, can they emulate the VM and all its (undocumented) platform features perfectly, so that no protection code can discriminate between the emulator and the real thing? So far, the answer is "no", and therefore, so far, BD+ remains "unbroken" in the most meaningful sense.
